source.dataset: NASA POWER (Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources)
source.method: Mann-Kendall trend test (two-sided) + Sen's slope, with autocorrelation correction: Hamed-Rao (1998) modified variance and Yue-Pilon pre-whitening. Source of every statistic below: mann-kendall-practice-2000-2025.md, computed from power-faisalabad-annual-2000-2025.csv.

usage: Paste this file into the app as the SINGLE source of truth for every number. The frontend chart, the verdict display, the demo and the chat/RAG must all read ONLY this file. If a user asks about a place, variable or period not in this file, the correct answer is 'not tested' — never a generated estimate. Do not round these numbers into different numbers in different places. Prepared Sat Nov 14, 2026, from the saved NASA POWER CSV and the autocorrelation-corrected Mann-Kendall practice run — no new data was collected for this file.

rainfall.headline: Don't trust it yet
rainfall.reason: Significant on 2000-2025 after correction and survives dropping 2020, but NOT significant on 2000-2019 alone (p = 0.23 uncorrected; 0.30 / 0.67 corrected). The rise is driven by the wet 2020s, not a steady 26-year climb — never present it as one.

verdicts.rule: Trust it = significant after correction AND survives dropping 2020. Don't trust it yet = significant on the full period only, NOT significant on 2000-2019 alone. Not significant = no claim.

temperature.headline: Don't trust it yet
temperature.reason: Significant on 2000-2025 after correction and survives dropping 2020, but NOT significant on 2000-2019 alone after correction (Hamed-Rao p = 0.056, Yue-Pilon p = 0.14). The cooling is also counterintuitive for Punjab and still needs a MODIS land-surface-temperature cross-check — the planner must NOT use it to relax heat planning.
